boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Hamilton College study environments, including library rooms with documented reservation guidance and campus academic spaces with specific study affordances.

cards.title: Burke Commons
cards.subtitle: Daniel Burke Library
cards.notes: Set up in the library’s named commons area for reading or laptop work; check the library’s room-reservation guidance before planning a group event.
cards.short_summary: A named common area inside Burke Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton’s Burke Library room-reservation page lists Burke Commons among its reservable library spaces.
cards.access_notes: Listed by the library as a reservable space; coordinate events with library personnel.

cards.title: All Night Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Daniel Burke Library
cards.notes: Use this named reading room for a focused library session, and confirm current building access arrangements with Hamilton before relying on it late.
cards.short_summary: A designated reading room in Burke Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton’s Burke Library room-reservation page identifies the All Night Reading Room as a library space.
cards.access_notes: The official page names the room but does not publish current daily access hours; verify access before visiting.

cards.title: Burke Library Study Room 209
cards.subtitle: Daniel Burke Library, second floor
cards.notes: Reserve Room 209 through 25Live for a study meeting, keeping the two-hour daily limit in mind when scheduling collaborators.
cards.short_summary: A reservable second-floor Burke Library study room.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton states that Burke Library Room 209 may be reserved through 25Live for study and meeting purposes.
cards.access_notes: Reservations are available Monday–Friday 4 p.m. to closing and weekends 10 a.m. to closing; individuals or groups are limited to two hours daily.

cards.title: Burke Library Study Room 211
cards.subtitle: Daniel Burke Library, second floor
cards.notes: Book Room 211 through 25Live when your study session needs a defined meeting space; submit same-day requests before the stated cutoff.
cards.short_summary: A reservable study and meeting room in Burke Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton states that Burke Library Room 211 may be reserved through 25Live for study and meeting purposes.
cards.access_notes: Same-day requests must arrive by 3 p.m.; reservations follow the page’s evening-and-weekend schedule and two-hour daily limit.

cards.title: Burke Library Study Room 213
cards.subtitle: Daniel Burke Library, second floor
cards.notes: Plan a short group work block in Room 213 and reserve it in 25Live rather than assuming the room will be open when you arrive.
cards.short_summary: A bookable Burke Library room for study or meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton states that Burke Library Room 213 may be reserved through 25Live for study and meeting purposes.
cards.access_notes: Available by reservation Monday–Friday 4 p.m. to closing and weekends 10 a.m. to closing; maximum two hours per day.

cards.title: Burke Library Study Room 215
cards.subtitle: Daniel Burke Library, second floor
cards.notes: Use 25Live to reserve Room 215 for a study meeting, and build a two-hour endpoint into your agenda before making the request.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor library study room with formal booking rules.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton states that Burke Library Room 215 may be reserved through 25Live for study and meeting purposes.
cards.access_notes: Available by reservation Monday–Friday 4 p.m. to closing and weekends 10 a.m. to closing; maximum two hours per day.

cards.title: Couper Classroom
cards.subtitle: Daniel Burke Library
cards.notes: For a structured academic gathering, ask a research librarian about reserving the Couper Classroom before setting a date or inviting participants.
cards.short_summary: A library classroom requiring librarian coordination.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton’s Burke Library page says reservations for the Couper Classroom must be coordinated with a research librarian.
cards.access_notes: Reservation must be coordinated with a research librarian; the page does not state drop-in study availability.

cards.title: Music Library
cards.subtitle: Lower level of McEwen Hall
cards.notes: Bring course listening or score work to this quiet, air-conditioned branch library; leave food and drinks outside because they are not permitted.
cards.short_summary: A quiet music-focused library with listening stations.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton describes the Music Library as a quiet, air-conditioned place to study or listen and says it has ten listening stations.
cards.access_notes: Located in McEwen’s lower level; food and drink are not permitted in the library.

cards.title: Kirner-Johnson Commons
cards.subtitle: Kirner-Johnson Building
cards.notes: Choose the KJ Commons when you want an indoor common area between classes, and use the building’s team rooms when your project needs collaboration.
cards.short_summary: A KJ common space paired with nearby team rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton identifies the Kirner-Johnson common space as a place to study and notes that the building includes team rooms for group projects.
cards.access_notes: The official facilities page describes common study space and team rooms but does not publish reservation or access rules.

cards.title: Taylor Science Center Atrium
cards.subtitle: Taylor Science Center
cards.notes: Use the large atrium gathering space for a campus-based work session, especially when you want to stay close to science classrooms and study rooms.
cards.short_summary: A large academic-building atrium near science study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton states that Taylor Science Center has a large atrium gathering space as well as student lounges and study rooms.
cards.access_notes: The facilities page documents the atrium and study rooms but does not publish public drop-in or reservation rules.
